examples.name: Selected (tone=default)
examples.description: tone=default keeps a visible border when selected, matching its own resting bordered look.

examples.name: Selected (tone=subtle)
examples.description: tone=subtle stays borderless when selected - the same background/text as tone=default's selected state, without a border, matching its own resting borderless look.

examples.name: With Tooltip
examples.description: Toggle Icon Button has no tooltip of its own, unlike Icon Button. Wrap it in Tooltip to show its name on hover and keyboard focus; aria-label stays the name.

examples.name: Controlled favorite
examples.description: The parent owns the state: isSelected comes from your state and onClick flips it. The name stays the same in both states; aria-pressed says whether it's on.

examples.name: Round and small
examples.description: shape is separate from tone: round is a full circle at every size. Sizes match Icon Button so the two line up in a toolbar.

antiExamples.name: Named only by a Tooltip
antiExamples.reason: A tooltip describes the button only while it shows, so the button has no accessible name. Name it with aria-label.

antiExamples.name: Changing the name with the state
antiExamples.jsx:
<ToggleIconButton
  aria-label={isFavorite ? 'Remove from favorites' : 'Add to favorites'}
  isSelected={isFavorite}
>
  <StarStarredIcon />
</ToggleIconButton>
antiExamples.reason: People hear "Remove from favorites, pressed" and can't tell what pressing does. Keep the name the same and let aria-pressed say whether it's on.

antiExamples.name: An unfamiliar icon
antiExamples.reason: An icon that isn't familiar on its own makes people guess. Use Toggle Button with a visible label when there's room.
